Ava: Heads-up — saw a 3–5x p95 regression on small-chat workloads after yesterday's batching change. Root looks like KV priming collisions when init (prefill) and gen (decode) both request KV warms in the same microbatch window.
Ravi: Ugh. Do we have a repro?
Miguel: Yes, I repro'd locally on rtx-pool: run the stress harness with --seq-dist=short and --burst=high. Attached perf counters show a KV stall spike at handshake.
Iris: Can you paste the perf snippet?
Miguel: 
```
perf record -e gpu_l2_cache_misses -c 100000 -o out.data -- ./bin/infer --model t5-xl --workload small-chat --concurrency 24
perf report -> kv_warm stall: 42% cycles
```
Ava: Interesting — kernel selection also flips between two small-attn kernels during handshake which might increase kernel launch overhead if batches are forming chaotically.
Ravi: So hypothesis: concurrent KV warms from both phases cause cache thrash + extra kernel churn. Two levers: (1) small grace period at batch formation to prefer phase-coalesced batches, (2) token-budget-aware gate so prefill cannot claim >X tokens in same batch as decode.
Iris: Love (1). How long of a grace? 200–500µs? If too long we hurt latency.
Miguel: I measured: 250µs gives 8% p95 improvement, 500µs 11%, but tail starts growing for low-rt workloads. We should make it adaptive: grace = min(500µs, 0.5 * avg-interarrival).
Ava: For (2) token gate, propose: if batch contains decode tokens > 8k (across reqs) then disallow prefill joins; otherwise allow. Simple and fast check.
Ravi: Need to be careful — some requests are mixed (initgen + streaming). Might need per-request phase tags and a soft-join score instead of hard block.
Iris: Another option: KV priming priority bit. Prefill requests set "kv-priority=low" and decode sets "kv-priority=high"; batch coordinator schedules warm ops ordered by that bit inside same kernel launch. Cheaper than full separation.
Miguel: That reduces collisions but not kernel flip churn. We saw kernel flip when sequence-length distribution within batch crosses threshold. Might help if we also prefer to group by approximate seq-len buckets before kernel selection.
Ava: OK action items:
- Miguel: run ablation with grace=adaptive and kv-priority bit, measure p50/p95/p99 and kernel-launch counts (due EOD).
- Ravi: sketch gating rules for token-budget soft-join (score function + thresholds).
- Iris: add a perf counter in the runtime to log "batch_kernel_count" and "kv_collisions" per 1s window.
perfbot: New perf test queued: job/kv-priming-probe-263987 (ETA ~15m) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Ravi: Also add an experiment where we sample 1% of batches and force prefill to wait one extra microbatch slot to emulate conservative join. Compare token cost and latency.
Miguel: FYI I saw a model-specific effect: models with Rotary scaling turned on have longer KV warm kernels; the same batching tweak gives bigger wins there. Will include per-model breakdown.
Iris: If we get >10% cost win for tail without regressing median, we can flip default.
Ava: Sounds good. If anyone hits a blocker ping me directly. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
